title: Early Warning Indicators and PIT vs TTC

maps.tested: Rated Very Important with no crash-course shortcut available, and reported in a consolidated recall.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'E.W.I.S.: point in time & through the cycle', appearing twice in the same list. Point-in-time ratings respond to current conditions and are volatile; through-the-cycle ratings are stressed-scenario-anchored and stable. The polarity of which is more procyclical is the trap.

vardeezReading: LTR-3: Very Important, "Full chapter is important". CR-6: Moderate, "CREDIT RATING AGENCY METHODOLOGIES (Just give a Good Read for This)". ORR-18: Very Important, with no note.

los.vardeez: Credit rating agency methodologies: give it a good read

selectors.name: Characteristics of sound EWIs
selectors.what: What makes an early warning indicator sound: leading (signals stress before the event, unlike lagging indicators such as GDP releases), sharp (granular, e.g. volatile deposit segments rather than total deposits) and with calibrated green, amber and red thresholds that are neither too wide nor so narrow that management is desensitised.

selectors.name: EWIs in the liquidity risk process
selectors.what: How EWIs are applied in liquidity risk management: breaches are escalated to the level with authority to act (corporate treasurer for modest buffer moves, ALCO for an asset-growth check after a large-outflow signal, the contingency funding plan for the most extreme cases), documented, and fed into reporting and the end-to-end framework.

selectors.name: PIT versus TTC definitions and users
selectors.what: Definitions and users of the two rating philosophies: TTC is long-term (at least one business cycle), robust and updated less often, used by the major rating agencies and for economic capital; PIT reflects current short-term conditions (usually within a year), is updated promptly and is used by banks' internal systems for short-term loans.

selectors.name: Trap: PIT is the procyclical, volatile one
selectors.what: The polarity question of which approach is more volatile and procyclical: PIT is volatile and more procyclical, while TTC is stable and reduces the volatility of economic capital; the flipped statement is the planted error. Includes the criticism that agency ratings claimed as TTC proved too optimistic in growth and too pessimistic in recessions.

selectors.name: Credit rating agency methodologies
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Credit rating agency methodologies: give it a good read'
